primitives.name: Resilience Coefficient
primitives.verbatim_quote: On the other hand, when a team of mine has run into an unexpected defeat in a practise game, I have an added confidence in it when it faces its next opponent.
primitives.assumptions: Post-defeat confidence increases monotonically with team's ability to recover from disruption.
primitives.breakdown_regime: R → 0 when defeat is expected or team fails to adapt.

layer2.mapping: Resilience coefficient maps to GSE state transition probability P(next_win | practice_loss), and to GSI posterior belief update on team strength.
layer2.telemetry: Observed win rate following practice-game defeat.

primitives.name: Memory-Weighted Performance
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the same way Princeton'memories will be apt tò recall the 1919 team rather than that of 1896 or 1903, simply because it came back after mid-season catastrophes and finished stronger than t began.
primitives.assumptions: Historical performance is weighted by recovery from adversity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: M → 0 when team fails to show improvement post-catastrophe.

layer2.mapping: Memory-weighted performance mirrors GSE trajectory reconstruction from disrupted states to final form; GSI uses this to infer latent team quality.
layer2.telemetry: Historical win-loss record adjusted for mid-season disruption severity.

primitives.name: Adaptive Competitiveness
primitives.verbatim_quote: Another feature of the practise games, socalled, is the fact that the modern system tends to lessen the handicap under which the smaller college used to play.
primitives.assumptions: Practice games reduce competitive imbalance between teams.
primitives.breakdown_regime: A → 1 when all teams are equally matched; A < 1 when disparity persists.

layer2.mapping: Adaptive competitiveness maps to GSE fairness-adjusted outcome prediction; GSI applies this to normalize variance in team strength estimates.
layer2.telemetry: Variance in team strength across practice vs. competitive seasons.

Resilience is modeled as a function of deviation from expected performance and subsequent adaptation. Memory-weighted performance reflects how past disruptions shape future perception, with emphasis on recovery. Adaptive competitiveness captures systemic changes in competition structure over time. These primitives form a triadic framework where resilience provides dynamic confidence, memory shapes perception, and adaptability adjusts competitive balance. Failure modes include: R=0 when teams do not recover, M=0 when teams fail to improve post-disruption, and A→0 when structural imbalance remains. Dualities emerge in how teams respond to defeat versus victory—defeat can signal either weakness or preparation. The operators are non-linear in their dependence on disruption magnitude and recovery time. The epistemological structure assumes that teams evolve through discrete state transitions governed by internal dynamics and external feedback loops.
